prose_changes.old: Two movements that had grown up separately in New England spent this century turning themselves into organized denominations. In 1819 William Ellery Channing preached an ordination sermon in Baltimore that gave liberal Congregationalists both a name and a platform, and in 1825 they founded the American Unitarian Association. The Universalists, who taught that God would in the end save everyone, built their own conventions on a separate track. Within a generation the Unitarian side produced a third thing it had not expected. Ralph Waldo Emerson left the ministry and told Harvard's divinity students in 1838 to look for religion in intuition and nature rather than historical revelation, and the Transcendentalists carried that further than most of their elders wanted to go. What held the movements together was less a shared creed than a shared refusal of creeds, along with a strong practical bent — toward schools, prisons, asylums and abolition.
prose_changes.new: Two movements had grown up apart in New England. In this century both grew into organized churches. By 1815 the liberal clergy of Boston's Congregational churches were already being called Unitarians. Many complaints were made that the label slandered them. In 1819 William Ellery Channing preached at an ordination in Baltimore. His sermon gave these liberals a platform. It also spoke out against the Trinity. In 1825 they founded the American Unitarian Association. The Universalists taught that God would in the end save everyone. They built their conventions on a track of their own. Within a generation the Unitarian side produced a third thing it had not looked for. Ralph Waldo Emerson left the ministry. In 1838 he told Harvard's divinity students to seek religion in their own souls and in nature. They were not to look for it in a revelation fixed in the past. The Transcendentalists took that further than most of their elders wanted to go. The two movements did not treat creeds alike. The Unitarians bound no one to a creed. The Universalists kept a short one, the Winchester Profession of 1803. In 1870 they made it a test of fellowship. Both had a strong practical bent. They worked hard for schools, prisons and asylums, and to end slavery.
